removed: --crf as an alias of --quality on every re-encoding tool that takes --quality (export.py keeps --crf: its preset chooses the encoder)
json and progress in the MCP inputSchema (they are CLI transport flags, not tool arguments)
probe's hdr meaning BT.2020 primaries or a PQ/HLG transfer
overwriting an existing output without --overwrite (1.x warned)
the result_v2 preview key and FFMPEG_SKILL_RESULT_V2 (the v1 top-level keys it was to replace were un-deprecated: they are the 2.0 shape)

toolMapLegend.json: flag: the tool takes --json and build_argv appends it; add: the tool takes --json but build_argv does not append it (MCP_JSON_EXEMPT), so the bridge passes json=True itself (look; also the doctor and contract handlers); native: the tool prints JSON without the flag (probe); none: no JSON output
toolMapLegend.brief: the tool supports --json-brief; detail=brief (defaultDetail) maps to json_brief=True
toolMapLegend.paths: param -> path role, see pathRoles; params not listed are not paths
toolMapLegend.required: always required (also in the manifest schema)
toolMapLegend.conditionalRequired: param is required when every rule holds: at least one of whenAny is truthy (when given) and none of whenNone is truthy (when given); enforced by the bridge only
toolMapLegend.choices: accepted values per param, numeric ones included (the manifest keeps only string enums)
toolMapLegend.mutuallyExclusive: at most one param of each group may be truthy
toolMapLegend.oneOfRequired: at least one param of each group must be truthy
toolMapLegend.constraints: relative_name: a file name or glob with no folder part and no '..'; lang_suffix: the value may end in :LANG (a language tag) after the path, so check the path part; jobs_cap: an integer string or 'auto', lowered to max
toolMapLegend.writesBesideInput: when param is truthy the tool writes next to the named input param, so that input's folder must be inside a write root
toolMapLegend.nested: the file holds more paths the bridge must check, relative to that file's own folder: brand_json (vendored _common.decision.BRAND_FILE_KEYS: logo, font_file; read), render_project (_common.decision.PROJECT_PATH_KEYS: output is written, the rest are read; plan documents refused), batch_recipe (output_dir is written; project is read; steps name upstream scripts with {in}/{out}), report_pack (the deliverables the pack table names; read)
toolMapLegend.removed: params refused by name with the reason given
toolMapLegend.deadline: per-tool wrapper deadline in seconds (null = the call deadline D)
toolMapLegend.handler: special handling in lib/bridge.py (render, batch, verify, doctor, contract); null = plain build_argv + run_tool

in_file.meaning: one existing file the tool reads
in_file.hint: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root).

in_files.meaning: a list of existing files the tool reads
in_files.hint: Existing input files (absolute, or relative to the output root).

in_dir.meaning: an existing folder the tool reads
in_dir.hint: Existing input folder (absolute, or relative to the output root).

in_paths.meaning: a list of existing files and/or folders the tool reads
in_paths.hint: Existing input files or folders (absolute, or relative to the output root).

out_file.meaning: the main file the tool writes; needs an extension; confined to the write roots
out_file.hint: Output file with an extension; a relative path lands in the output root.

out_side_file.meaning: an extra file the tool writes when named; confined to the write roots
out_side_file.hint: Extra file to write; a relative path lands in the output root.

out_dir.meaning: a folder the tool writes into; confined to the write roots
out_dir.hint: Output folder; a relative path lands in the output root.

dropEverywhere.argv: raw CLI arguments are not accepted; use the named parameters
dropEverywhere.json: set by the wrapper; use detail instead
dropEverywhere.json_brief: set by the wrapper; use detail instead
dropEverywhere.progress: progress events are not supported by Sophon skills
dropEverywhere.plan: plan files are not supported; use dry_run to see the commands
dropEverywhere.hw: GPU (Apple VideoToolbox) switching is not exposed; encodes run on the CPU
dropEverywhere.no_hw: GPU (Apple VideoToolbox) switching is not exposed; encodes run on the CPU

readOnlyDrop.overwrite: this read-only tool writes no file

commonDescriptions.dry_run: Plan only: return the ffmpeg commands that would run and write nothing (tools that measure still read the input).
commonDescriptions.timeout: Seconds one ffmpeg run may take (default 1800); the wrapper lowers it to fit the call's own deadline.
commonDescriptions.overwrite: Replace an existing output. Honoured only when every output is inside the output root; anywhere else the call is refused.
commonDescriptions.fast: Preview quality (x264 veryfast) for quick iterations; leave it off for the final file.

detail.description: brief (default): a compact result. full: the whole upstream JSON document; a very large one is saved to a report file and its path returned.

project_json.description: The project as inline JSON text (at most 64 KB) instead of a project file; it is saved under the output root's projects/ folder and rendered from there, so use absolute paths inside it.

use_cache.description: Reuse stages that did not change since an earlier render of the same project (cache kept in the output root). Turn it on for re-renders after small fixes.

recipe_json.description: The batch recipe as inline JSON text (at most 64 KB) instead of a recipe file; use absolute paths inside it.

tool_name.description: The tool to describe: a full name such as ffmpeg.edit.cut, or the upstream script name such as cut. Omit it for a one-line summary of every tool.

probe.useWhen: Use first on every input you plan from, and to confirm a written file: duration, size, fps, codecs, audio streams, HDR.

cropdetect.useWhen: Use before ffmpeg.adjust.crop when a source shows black bars.

check.useWhen: Use as the last step before delivery: PASS/WARN/FAIL rows against a platform (reels, shorts, tiktok, youtube ...), each naming its fix.

scenes.useWhen: Use to plan cuts in long footage; it can also measure a beat grid (beats), shot types (shots) and write a contact sheet (sheet).

look.useWhen: Use after any picture change to see the result: a PNG contact sheet, frames at given times or a side-by-side; then inspect the PNG.

descriptions.output: Output PNG with an extension (the sheet or compare image, or the base name for at frames); a relative path lands in the output root.

report.useWhen: Use to hand a finished video to someone who wants one file to review.

insert.useWhen: Use to bring a still image (generated or supplied) into a timeline as a clip of exact length, with optional Ken Burns zoom and pan.

background.useWhen: Use for title-card, spacer or end-card backgrounds of a given size and length.

sequence.useWhen: Use when the frames already exist as numbered or globbed images in one folder.

pattern.text: A file name pattern inside dir; no folder part.

waveform.useWhen: Use to turn a voice-over, podcast or music track into a video: a waveform or spectrum over a colour or still image, optionally captioned.

cut.useWhen: Use to trim a clip (start, end or duration) or to keep or drop several ranges (segments, remove); lossless when keyframes allow.

join.useWhen: Use to put two or more clips in order with fade, dissolve, wipe or slide transitions.

removed.list: pass the clips in inputs; a clip-list file would name paths the wrapper cannot check

silence.useWhen: Use to tighten talking-head or podcast footage by removing pauses (and filler words with a transcript), or only to list them.

broll.useWhen: Use to show other footage over a main clip for a while (cutaways) without changing the main clip's timing or sound.

multicam.useWhen: Use for two or more cameras of the same take: aligns them by sound, then cuts between them by a switch list or by loudness.

sync.useWhen: Use to find the offset between a camera and an external recorder, and optionally write the synced file.

grid.useWhen: Use for split screens and video walls: several clips or stills side by side in a columns x rows grid.

pad.useWhen: Use to add black, silent time before or after a clip.

freeze.useWhen: Use for an end-card hold or a pause on one frame.

loop.useWhen: Use to repeat a short clip a number of times or up to a length, with a crossfade or boomerang at the seams.

metadata.useWhen: Use to add chapters (from a file, or proposed from pauses and scene changes) and title or artist tags without re-encoding.

fit.useWhen: Use to reach a platform aspect (9:16, 1:1, 16:9) by pad, crop or blurred fill, to change length by speed or trim, or to resize, rotate or flip.

crop.useWhen: Use when you know the exact rectangle to keep, for example from ffmpeg.inspect.cropdetect.

color.summary: Colour management: HDR (PQ, HLG) to SDR BT.709 with real tone mapping, a .cube LUT, colour-tag fixes without re-encoding, or typed primary correction (exposure, contrast, saturation, gamma, white balance, lift/gain, levels, curves).
color.useWhen: Use for HDR phone footage going to SDR platforms, Log footage, a .cube look, or exposure and white-balance fixes.

speedramp.useWhen: Use for speed-ramp effects: different constant speeds over consecutive ranges that cover the whole clip.

reverse.useWhen: Use for a rewind effect; the whole clip is held in memory, so keep it short.

straighten.useWhen: Use to level a tilted horizon by a small angle (-45 to 45 degrees).

sphere.useWhen: Use to get a normal flat shot out of 360-degree footage, choosing the direction and field of view.

stabilize.useWhen: Use for shaky handheld footage; needs an FFmpeg build with libvidstab and is slow.

deinterlace.useWhen: Use when moving edges show comb lines.

redact.useWhen: Use to hide a face, number plate or logo that stays in one fixed rectangle for the whole clip.

caption.useWhen: Use to burn in or attach subtitles from an SRT/ASS file or a plain cue file (one 'start-end text' line per cue), with animation, karaoke and platform safe zones.

graphics.useWhen: Use for designed text on video: hook cards, titles, lower thirds, chapter cards, progress bars, countdowns, stickers, memes.

overlay.useWhen: Use to place a logo, an image, a text line or a second video (picture-in-picture, green screen) on a clip, with timing, fade and opacity.

audio.useWhen: Use to clean a voice, add a music bed that ducks under speech, add effects, replace or extract the sound, or change channels or sample rate.

loudness.useWhen: Use to hit a platform loudness target (-14 LUFS for streaming by default) before export, or only to measure it.

descriptions.versions: Write one normalised file per target (comma list: streaming, ebu-r128, broadcast-jp or LUFS/TP pairs such as -16/-1.5). The files are written next to the input, so the input must be inside the output root.

export.useWhen: Use as the final encode for a platform or a master (youtube, reels, tiktok, shorts, prores, dnxhr, gif ...); can also aim at a file size.

proxy.useWhen: Use to make a light copy of heavy footage (4K, HEVC, ProRes) for quick looks and tests.

render.useWhen: Use for any edit of three or more steps: one project (clips, transitions, captions, graphics, overlays, music, loudness, export, check) in one call, or a platform template on one video.
render.writes: Writes: the project's output, or output in template mode; work files stay in the call's temp folder. Relative output paths land in the output root.

removed.work: the wrapper keeps intermediates in the call's own temp folder
removed.keep: intermediates are always removed after the call
removed.audit_log: audit logs are not written by the wrapper
removed.cache: use use_cache; the cache folder lives in the output root

descriptions.project: Existing input file (absolute, or relative to the output root): a project.json to render, or with template the video to deliver.
descriptions.output: Output file with an extension; a relative path lands in the output root. Template mode only (a project names its own output); for a template list or all, its folder receives the pack.

batch.useWhen: Use to apply the same steps or project to every file in a folder; a content-hash cache skips files that were already done.
batch.writes: Writes: into the recipe's output_dir, which must be inside the write roots (relative = under the output root).

removed.watch: watching a folder would block the call; run batch again instead
removed.work: the wrapper keeps intermediates in the call's own temp folder

verify.useWhen: Use once on a new machine or with unusual footage to prove every step works on it; its outputs go to a fresh folder in the output root.
verify.writes: Writes: test outputs into a fresh folder in the output root; the report file when named.

removed.out: the wrapper picks a fresh folder in the output root
removed.keep: the wrapper keeps the outputs in the output root
removed.dry_run: verify always runs real encodes; it has no dry run

descriptions.timeout: Seconds each verification step may take (default 600); the wrapper lowers it to fit the call's own deadline.

doctor.summary: Check this computer: Python, FFmpeg and ffprobe versions, the filters, encoders, fonts and speech engines each tool needs, and where the skill writes (outputRoot).
doctor.useWhen: Use once per session before the first edit, and after a dependency error; relay each problem's fix to the user.

contract.summary: Describe the tools: every parameter of one tool with its flags, defaults and accepted values, or a one-line summary of all of them.
contract.useWhen: Use when a parameter's meaning or accepted values are unclear.
